Use on /done, or when wrapping up a session where nothing remains to resume or the continuation prompt already exists (a standup queue's next item). Runs the handoff close-out minus the resume-prompt step. Need a fresh resume prompt? Use handoff instead, never both. In a parent session it closes the child sessions first.

skills.name: explain
skills.description: Re-explain the last message in plain words, using the project's own vocabulary.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Discover and install agent skills. Use only when the user explicitly asks for a skill ("find or install a skill for X", "is there a skill that..."), never for an ordinary how-do-I question.

skills.name: first-customers
skills.description: Find and reach a product's first customers honestly: demand signals, local-business prospect lists, outreach drafts a human sends. Use when asking "who would buy this" or "how do I get my first users or clients". Offer and positioning are marketing; wording is plain-language.

skills.name: frontend
skills.description: Frontend structure and behavior: components, state, a typed service layer, lists, tables and filters, forms, modals, loading/empty/error states, routing, SSR, web performance. Use when building or refactoring UI or adding any screen. Vue 3 + Tabler today, framework-agnostic in approach. Tabler specifics are tabler-ui; visual judgment is design-guide; content placement is information-architecture.

skills.name: git-sync
skills.description: The standing git workflow. Use at the start of any branch work and before every commit, push, rebase or PR: your own branch (never main), rebased on current main, every branch pushed, PR bodies in the standard shape, PRs reported only when green, and merged branches and worktrees pruned before a session ends.

skills.name: grant-writing
skills.description: Research grant applications: research and mentoring plans, specific aims, budget justifications, abstracts. Use when writing or strengthening a proposal, checking a draft against a funder's guidelines or review criteria, or responding to reviewers. Owns proposal strategy and structure; wording is academic-writing, study design is research-methods.

skills.name: handoff
skills.description: Durable session handoff with a resume prompt. Use when pausing or ending work at a real boundary (a phase or PR done, a blocker, a pivot, a drained queue) or when the user says "hand off" or "we'll continue later". Saves state outside the chat plus an exact resume point, never just a chat summary. No new resume prompt needed? Use done.

skills.name: i18n
skills.description: Multi-language support (i18n/l10n). Use when a task touches a translation file or a user-facing string in a product that ships more than one language: adding a language or key, extracting strings, vue-i18n/nestjs-i18n/go-i18n, locale formatting, translated data (enums, emails, PDFs), locale routing, hreflang, RTL. Its core failure is a key that reaches one pack and not the others.

skills.name: idea-refine
skills.description: Turn a vague idea into a sharp, actionable concept by diverging, then converging. Use for pure ideation: "ideate", "refine this idea", "explore options for X". It sits upstream of a plan; to plan an idea already chosen, use planning.

skills.name: information-architecture
skills.description: How content and pages are organized for their audience: site maps, page inventories, each page's job, where a message or feature lives, navigation and funnels, heading structure, buried or orphaned messages. Applies to docs, books, curricula and papers too. Use when outlining, when adding or reordering pages or sections, and on any content-page review. Looks are design-guide; wording is plain-language or academic-writing.

skills.name: infrastructure
skills.description: Change infrastructure and dev-workflow tooling: Nomad, Consul, Vault, Terraform, Docker, GitHub Actions, task runners, env and direnv setup, setup scripts, a project's own ops CLI, launchd and hooks. Use when editing any of these or debugging env or worktree setup. Looking up how to run a project is project-config; third-party APIs are integrations.

skills.name: integrations
skills.description: Connect to or automate third-party services: REST APIs, MCP servers, OAuth and tokens, webhooks, recurring syncs. Use when building or debugging an integration, scheduling a job against an external service, deciding where automation runs, making external writes idempotent, or researching a vendor API. Internal service-to-service calls are service-architecture.

skills.name: marketing
skills.description: Why people choose, buy, sign up and stay, applied honestly: behavioral models, offers, pricing, trust, urgency, onboarding and growth loops for the apps and sites we build. Use when shaping a landing, pricing, signup or launch page, an offer or free tier, or asking "why would anyone pick this". Wording is plain-language; page structure is information-architecture.

skills.name: monitoring
skills.description: Observability into running code. Use when adding logging or instrumentation, diagnosing a running service ("watch the logs", "what is it actually doing"), standardizing log output, or when a change must be proven on the live app because tests can't reach it. Deploy and alerting stacks are infrastructure; tests are tdd-skill.

skills.name: orchestration
skills.description: Run multi-step or long-running work as an orchestrator over disposable sub-agents. Use at the start of a program phase, migration, broad sweep, deep research or many-file job, or when your context fills with exploration. Not for single-step edits or quick questions.

skills.name: plain-language
skills.description: Clear, friendly, jargon-free writing for non-technical readers: ticket text, QA steps, release notes, status updates, UI copy, business messages. Use when writing for QA, product, stakeholders or end users, or on a "make this less technical" pass. Scholarly prose is academic-writing; document structure is information-architecture.

skills.name: planning
skills.description: Plan before building anything non-trivial: multi-file or multi-phase work, a feature, a migration, or whenever asked to plan. Research, write the plan, ask every decision up front (a second gate only for questions that depend on a first-gate answer), get approval, then execute autonomously. No implementation while the approval gate is open.

skills.name: project-config
skills.description: The recorded facts of how each project runs: node version, env and direnv, package manager, monorepo layout, and the exact install, run, build, test, lint and migrate commands. Consult before your first shell command in a repo and before briefing an agent that will run one. Record any missing fact the moment you find it.

skills.name: project-manager
skills.description: Keep the tracker (Jira, Trello, or GitHub Issues and Projects) in sync with the real work. Use on /project-manager or "file a ticket", "is this tracked", "write QA steps", "audit my tickets", "find duplicates", "clean up the backlog". Drafts every change and asks before writing to the tracker. Working your assigned tickets is standup.

skills.name: research-methods
skills.description: Social and health research design: conceptual and logic models, CBPR/YPAR, participatory and agent-based modeling, spatial indices, implementation frameworks (CFIR, RE-AIM), measures, IRB and human-subjects sections, literature synthesis. Use when planning a study or choosing a method or framework. Proposal structure is grant-writing; wording is academic-writing.

skills.name: security-and-hardening
skills.description: Security standards a default pass gets wrong: credential reach, proving a control holds, leak-free secret scanning, SSRF/TOCTOU, deployment topology. Use when handling untrusted input, auth, sessions, stored data or third-party calls; adding or upgrading a dependency; pinning Actions or base images; editing CI, Dockerfiles or hooks; wiring an MCP server; or when the secret-scan hook denies a commit. Run the review itself with /security-review.

skills.name: service-architecture
skills.description: Backend architecture decisions: service boundaries, splitting vs consolidating, inter-service calls, auth guards and tiers, where logic lives, strangler migrations. Load before adding or versioning an endpoint or a service-to-service call, or deciding which service owns something. Query performance is database-optimization.

skills.name: source-driven-development
skills.description: Ground implementation decisions in official documentation, with citations. Use when building with a framework or library where correctness matters or common patterns may be outdated.

skills.name: status-update
skills.description: Session status as a visual dashboard plus a 2-3 line TLDR, never prose alone. Use on /status-update, "where are we", "what's left", mid-way through a multi-item run, and at any wrap-up covering more than one unit of work.

skills.name: tabler-ui
skills.description: Tabler admin template (tabler.io) components and the workarounds that make them behave in Vue 3. Consult before any Tabler markup or interactive component: modals, dropdowns, badges, grids, forms, icons, wizards, empty states, emails. Structure is frontend; visual judgment is design-guide.

skills.name: tdd-skill
skills.description: Test-first (red-green-refactor) for any codebase. Use when adding or changing behavior, fixing a bug (it starts with a failing regression test), or asked to add or cover tests. Finds how this project runs tests, names the seams under test, and verifies on a live stack when a unit test can't reach the behavior. Watching an existing change run is /verify.

agents.name: literature-scout

agents.name: source-acquirer

agents.name: source-ingester

Reads ONE source PDF/text under a specific focus and produces a focus-driven Source page + entity pages + BibTeX entry + log line. Re-ingest of an existing source page appends a new focus block rather than overwriting. Fresh context per dispatch.

agents.name: wiki-linter
